Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes after canary swap (urgent)

Ben —

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 latency around 08:30 PDT after your team flipped the canary for model v3.0. Sample metrics from our side (US region): p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~780ms; p99 is now ~1.9s. Throughput is fine but error rate is creeping up to 0.7% (timeouts). This is impacting our synchronous user flows.

Attached is a small trace sample and the timestamps where we saw the degradation. Can someone from infra/engineers join a quick call? We need this prioritized — it started right after the A/B switch.

CJ

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes after canary swap (urgent)

On Fri, May 14, 2027 at 09:31, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Dylan, can you confirm if there were kernel or quantization-path changes in v3.0 that would increase tail latency for the 1k-2k token sequences Brightbridge uses?

Checked logs and the canary diff. Summary: v3.0 enabled an experimental attention-kernel fallback for sequences >1024 (to support a multi-head config change). For typical short requests this is neutral, but for Brightbridge’s longer prompt profile it triggers extra memcpy and scalar fallback code paths — causing increased KV cache misses and tail latency amplification under concurrent batches.

What I see in the attached microtrace: token generation stalls for ~700–1000ms during KV window reallocation, which aligns with the p95 jump. CPU utilization on the host is normal; latency is kernel-path dominated.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by speed/risk):
- Roll back the canary to v2.7 (fastest; requires routing change, ~2–5m to take effect).
- Reduce v3.0 traffic to 1% and hold while we patch fallback path (medium).
- Apply a hotfix to skip the fallback for sequences <2048 (requires a build + deploy, ~3–4h).

I recommend rollback to v2.7 now, collect stable traces, and schedule a hotfix. I’ll attach the config diff we used for the canary.

Dylan
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Update: we rolled Brightbridge back to hosted-model:v2.7 at 11:19 PDT and monitored the panel. p95 returned to ~210–250ms and p99 dropped under 500ms within the 20-minute stabilization window. Error rate normalized to ~0.02%.

Root cause (preliminary): a fallback attention kernel path in v3.0 that behaves poorly for 1k+ token sequences under our batching heuristics. Dylan will lead a targeted fix and we’ll keep you posted on timeline.

Goodwill: Evelyn approved one month of credits; Marissa will send the formal note/credit schedule.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll post a postmortem and a plan to prevent similar regressions on future canaries (better sequence-profile gating + tighter canary caps).

If you want a short wrap-up call tomorrow to walk through the trace and follow-ups, I’m available 09:30–11:00 PDT.
